text: Reuse / clone on existing transitions; distinct substrings.

A general suffix automaton (广义后缀自动机) accepts every substring of several strings at once. Insert the strings one after another, restarting from the root each time; but when the transition for the next character already exists, do not create a new state: reuse it, or clone it if its length is wrong. Without that check the automaton gets duplicate, unreachable states and counts go wrong (P6139).

Equivalent safe construction: build a trie of all strings, then add trie nodes to the SAM in BFS order, each extending from its parent's state. Distinct substrings of all strings = Σ (len[v] − len[link[v]]), as for one string (拓展篇第3章). Keeping, per state, which strings reach it answers "substrings common to k strings".
bbbbaaa abbbab aaababab baba bbbbbba abbb

Distinct substrings over all strings, checked against putting every substring of every string into a Python set. Strings that are prefixes of each other ("abab" and "ab…") are where the reuse branch matters.

The bug to avoid: plain extend after resetting last = 0 creates a fresh state even when the transition exists, so a string seen before gets a second, disconnected state. That is exactly what the first branch of extend() prevents.

Typical problems: count substrings that occur in at least k of the strings (mark each state with the strings that reach it while walking each string); 诸神眷顾的幻想乡(P3346) builds the general SAM of all root-to- leaf paths of a tree with at most 20 leaves.
